author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. national average for diesel rose above $6 a gallon Friday, extending a record run that is increasing costs for trucking, farming and delivery networks. AAA put the average near $6.06, up from $5.85 a week earlier and about $3.71 at the same point last year.

Diesel prices generally track crude oil and refined-fuel markets. Brent and U.S. crude both moved above $100 a barrel during the week as conflict and shipping disruptions constrained supply. Diesel is particularly sensitive because it powers much of the freight system, as well as farm equipment and some public transportation.

The market impact reaches beyond fuel retailers. Businesses that move packages or perishable food may absorb the increase, add delivery fees or eventually pass costs into consumer prices. Refrigerated products such as meat and produce can face pressure sooner because they require frequent transport and restocking. The figures are a national snapshot reported for September 11, not a live local quote; pump prices vary by state and station. The persistence of high crude and refining costs will determine how much of the diesel surge reaches broader inflation measures.
dek: AAA’s September 11 national average was nearly $6.06, up about 63% from a year earlier and adding pressure across freight networks.
headline: U.S. diesel average tops $6 as freight costs face pressure
